exposure: sequential use of rotation and traction forceps
cohort: The study included patients who underwent instrumental delivery from January 2017 to April 2022.
finding: There were no significant differences in the presence of OASIS comparing traction and rotation forceps, though a non-significant trend of higher OASIS was observed following the sequential use of rotation and traction forceps.
mod_finding: No significant differences in OASIS incidence were found between rotation and traction forceps, but a non-significant trend of higher OASIS was observed with the sequential use of both types of forceps during instrumental delivery.
